es.summary: Protrusión de la parte superior del estómago a través del hiato esofágico del diafragma, facilitando el reflujo gastroesofágico.
key_points: Debilidad del hiato permite que el estómago suba al tórax.
Factores de riesgo: edad >50 años, obesidad y tabaquismo.
Síntomas típicos: pirosis, regurgitación, disfagia y tos seca.
Diagnóstico mediante radiografía, estudio con bario y endoscopia.
Tratamiento inicial: cambios de estilo de vida y antiácidos.
Complicaciones: esofagitis, esófago de Barrett y aspiración pulmonar.

pathophysiology: Debilidad o apertura del hiato esofágico del diafragma permite protrusión gástrica al tórax.
La válvula gastroesofágica inferior pierde presión de cierre, favoreciendo el reflujo ácido.
El ácido irrita el epitelio esofágico, provocando inflamación y síntomas de GERD.
Presión intraabdominal aumentada (obesidad, tabaquismo) agrava la hernia.
signs_symptoms: Disfagia o sensación de cuerpo extraño al tragar.
Dolor torácico que puede confundirse con angina.
diagnostics: Radiografía de tórax: aire por encima del diafragma.
Estudio con bario (esofagografía): visualiza hernia y reflujo.
Endoscopia digestiva alta: evalúa esofagitis y estenosis.
pH‑metría esofágica: pH <4 >4% del tiempo indica GERD.
Hemograma: descartar anemia por sangrado crónico.
treatment: Elevación de cabecera 30‑45° durante y 2‑3 h después de comer.
Comidas pequeñas y frecuentes; evitar alimentos grasos, cafeína, alcohol y chocolate.
Antiácidos (hidróxido de aluminio, carbonato de calcio) para alivio rápido.
Inhibidores de bomba de protones (omeprazol) o bloqueadores H2 (ranitidina) para control a largo plazo.
Fundoplicatura laparoscópica cuando los síntomas son refractarios.
complications: Aspiración pulmonar y neumonía por reflujo.
Dolor torácico crónico que puede limitar la actividad.
nursing_care: Evaluar frecuencia e intensidad de pirosis y regurgitación cada turno.
Monitorear signos de aspiración: tos, cambios en auscultación y saturación de O₂.
Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos; vigilar peso diario.
Mantener al paciente en posición semisentada durante y después de las comidas.
Administrar antiácidos y PPIs según prescripción; observar alivio de síntomas.
Educar sobre medidas de estilo de vida y signos de complicaciones.
patient_teaching: Comer porciones pequeñas y evitar comer 2‑3 h antes de acostarse.
Elevar la cabecera de la cama 30‑45° y dormir en posición izquierda.
Perder peso gradualmente y evitar el tabaco y el alcohol.
Limitar alimentos irritantes: fritos, picantes, cítricos y chocolate.
Tomar antiácidos o PPIs según indicación y no interrumpir el tratamiento sin consultar.
Reportar tos persistente, dolor torácico nuevo o vómitos con sangre.

outcomes: Mantener vía aérea libre: sin episodios de aspiración durante la hospitalización

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de aspiración (tos, cambios en auscultación) cada turno
interventions.rationale: Permite detección temprana y prevención de complicaciones respiratorias

interventions.action: Mantener al paciente en posición semisentada (30‑45°) durante y después de las comidas
interventions.rationale: Reduce el reflujo y el riesgo de que contenido gástrico sea aspirado

interventions.action: Administrar antiácidos según indicación y observar alivio de síntomas
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la acidez que favorece la irritación y aspiración

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de deglución segura y evitar alimentos irritantes
interventions.rationale: Previene ingreso de contenido al tracto respiratorio

interventions.action: Monitorear saturación de O₂ y auscultar pulmones cada 4 horas
interventions.rationale: Detecta deterioro respiratorio precozmente

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Ingesta de líquidos ≥ 2 L/día mantenida durante la estancia

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno
interventions.rationale: Identifica déficit de volumen y guía la reposición

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos en pequeñas cantidades frecuentes
interventions.rationale: Mejora tolerancia y reduce episodios de vómito

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de deshidratación (turgor, mucosas, frecuencia cardíaca)
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana ante pérdida de líquidos

interventions.action: Administrar antieméticos según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Controla náuseas y facilita la ingesta adecuada

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre importancia de hidratación y alimentos blandos
interventions.rationale: Promueve autocuidado y previene complicaciones por deshidratación

en.summary: Protrusion of the upper stomach through the esophageal hiatus of the diaphragm, facilitating gastroesophageal reflux.
key_points: Weakness of the hiatus allows the stomach to rise into the chest.
Risk factors: age >50 years, obesity, and smoking.
Typical symptoms: heartburn, regurgitation, dysphagia, and dry cough.
Diagnosis via X‑ray, barium study, and endoscopy.
Initial treatment: lifestyle changes and antacids.
Complications: esophagitis, Barrett’s esophagus, and pulmonary aspiration.

pathophysiology: Weakness or opening of the diaphragmatic esophageal hiatus allows gastric protrusion into the chest.
The lower esophageal sphincter loses closing pressure, favoring acid reflux.
Acid irritates the esophageal epithelium, causing inflammation and GERD symptoms.
Increased intraabdominal pressure (obesity, smoking) worsens the hernia.
signs_symptoms: Dysphagia or sensation of a foreign body when swallowing.
Chest pain that may mimic angina.
diagnostics: Chest X‑ray: air above the diaphragm.
Barium study (esophagography): visualizes hernia and reflux.
Upper endoscopy: evaluates esophagitis and stenosis.
Esophageal pH monitoring: pH <4 >4% of time indicates GERD.
CBC: rule out anemia from chronic bleeding.
treatment: Elevate head 30‑45° during and 2‑3 h after meals.
Small, frequent meals; avoid fatty foods, caffeine, alcohol, and chocolate.
Antacids (aluminum hydroxide, calcium carbonate) for rapid relief.
Proton‑pump inhibitors (omeprazole) or H2 blockers (ranitidine) for long‑term control.
Laparoscopic fundoplication when symptoms are refractory.
complications: Pulmonary aspiration and pneumonia from reflux.
Chronic chest pain that may limit activity.
nursing_care: Assess frequency and intensity of heartburn and regurgitation each shift.
Monitor for aspiration signs: cough, changes in auscultation, and O₂ saturation.
Record intake and output; monitor daily weight.
Keep patient in semi‑upright position during and after meals.
Administer antacids and PPIs as prescribed; observe symptom relief.
Educate on lifestyle measures and signs of complications.
patient_teaching: Eat small portions and avoid eating 2‑3 h before bedtime.
Elevate head of bed 30‑45° and sleep on left side.
Lose weight gradually and avoid tobacco and alcohol.
Limit irritant foods: fried, spicy, citrus, and chocolate.
Take antacids or PPIs as directed and do not stop treatment without consulting.
Report persistent cough, new chest pain, or vomiting with blood.

outcomes: Maintain airway clear: no aspiration episodes during hospitalization

interventions.action: Assess aspiration signs (cough, auscultation changes) each shift
interventions.rationale: Allows early detection and prevention of respiratory complications

interventions.action: Keep patient semi‑upright (30‑45°) during and after meals
interventions.rationale: Reduces reflux and risk of gastric content aspiration

interventions.action: Administer antacids as ordered and observe symptom relief
interventions.rationale: Decreases acidity that favors irritation and aspiration

interventions.action: Teach safe swallowing techniques and avoid irritant foods
interventions.rationale: Prevents entry of content into the respiratory tract

interventions.action: Monitor O₂ saturation and auscultate lungs every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early respiratory deterioration

outcomes: Fluid intake ≥ 2 L/day maintained during stay

interventions.action: Record intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Identifies volume deficit and guides replacement

interventions.action: Offer fluids in small frequent amounts
interventions.rationale: Improves tolerance and reduces vomiting episodes

interventions.action: Assess dehydration signs (turgor, mucous membranes, heart rate)
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention for fluid loss

interventions.action: Administer antiemetics as prescribed
interventions.rationale: Controls nausea and facilitates adequate intake

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of hydration and soft foods
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and prevents dehydration complications

summary.0.quote: A hiatal hernia is a condition in which the upper part of your stomach bulges through an opening in your diaphragm.

key_points.1.quote: Your risk of getting a hiatal hernia goes up as you age; they are common in people over age 50.

key_points.2.quote: GERD may cause symptoms such as : Heartburn Problems swallowing A dry cough Bad breath Nausea and/or vomiting Breathing problems The wearing away of your teeth

key_points.3.quote: The tests may be a chest x-ray, an x-ray with a barium swallow, or an upper endoscopy.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: A hiatal hernia is a condition in which the upper part of your stomach bulges through an opening in your diaphragm.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Your risk of getting a hiatal hernia goes up as you age; they are common in people over age 50.

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: GERD may cause symptoms such as : Heartburn Problems swallowing A dry cough Bad breath Nausea and/or vomiting Breathing problems The wearing away of your teeth Often, the cause of a hiatal hernia is unknown.

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: GERD may cause symptoms such as : Heartburn Problems swallowing A dry cough Bad breath Nausea and/or vomiting Breathing problems The wearing away of your teeth Often, the cause of a hiatal hernia is unknown.

sections.treatment.2.quote: Calcium carbonate is a fast-acting oral antacid that efficiently neutralizes gastric acids, offering relief from heartburn and associated symptoms.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: They include eating small meals, avoiding certain foods, not smoking or drinking alcohol, and losing weight.
